subject: Audit log extraction feasibility — Scyphos follow-up & questionnaire
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@scyphoshealth.com>
Cc: security@scyphoshealth.com, procurement <procurement@scyphoshealth.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Audit log extraction feasibility — Scyphos follow-up & questionnaire

Hi Lina — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our call so your security and procurement teams have a clear path forward.

Summary of what we covered:
- Admin activity logs: event-level change history (user, action, timestamp, object id) exposed via API and bulk export.
- API request/response logs: request headers, route, response codes, latencies — we discussed sampling vs full retention.
- Export modalities: real-time streaming to customer S3 vs periodic bulk export (daily/weekly) as JSONL or CSV.
- Immutability/WORM: you flagged the requirement for tamper-evidence for at least 90 days; we discussed write-once cloud storage patterns.

Outstanding questions (would appreciate answers from security/procurement):
1) Required retention window for admin & API logs (regulatory vs forensic).
2) Immutability threshold (90 days?). Is legal asking for longer?
3) Preferred export format: JSONL (recommended) or CSV?
4) Access pattern for exports: ad-hoc retrieval vs on-demand API retrieval SLA (minutes/hours).
5) Any encryption/KMS constraints for exported archives?

Next steps:
- I attached a short preliminary questionnaire (scyphos_audit_questions.xlsx) that captures the items above plus formats and delivery preferences. Can security@scyphoshealth.com please fill those out and return by EOD next Tuesday (2027-07-02)?
- On our side, I'll create a sample export (anonymized) and a short config snippet showing S3 + server-side-encryption + object lock for immutability.
- Propose a technical touchpoint (30m) next week with our infra solutions engineer to review the sample export and answer detailed questions.

Attachments: scyphos_audit_questions.xlsx (questionnaire), redwood_export_instructions.txt (config snippet)

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

---
Note: this thread contains a mix of sales and technical items; happy to loop in our security PM if you want an attestation on SOC 2 scope for logging.

From: Lina Torres <lina.torres@scyphoshealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: security@scyphoshealth.com, procurement <procurement@scyphoshealth.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit log extraction feasibility — Scyphos follow-up & questionnaire

Thanks Ben — that was a helpful call. A few clarifications from our side (security team responding):

> On Fri, Jun 25, 2027 at 4:10 PM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> > - Admin activity logs: event-level change history (user, action, timestamp, object id) exposed via API and bulk export.
> > - API request/response logs: request headers, route, response codes, latencies — we discussed sampling vs full retention.
>
We can confirm the following priorities:
- SOC 2: we are SOC 2 in-scope for our product, but still completing remediation. We need evidence that logs are exportable and immutable for the 90-day baseline during SOC testing.
- HIPAA: Scyphos is a HIPAA-covered entity; audit trails for user access and configuration changes are required for 2 years.
- Retention: for admin logs we require 2 years, but we would like a short-term hot window (30 days) for quick queries and a cold archive for the rest.
- Immutability: object-lock / WORM for 90 days is minimum; legal is assessing whether 2 years is preferable.
- Export format: JSONL preferred; CSV ok for simple tables, but we will need schemas for each event type.
- Delivery: prefer daily bulk export to our S3 bucket with server-side encryption and SSE-KMS keys that we control.

Action items from us: security@ will complete your questionnaire and return by next Tue (2027-07-02). Procurement will follow up with contract and SOW constraints after the technical sample is validated.

Thanks —
Lina Torres
Head of Product Security
Scyphos Health
lina.torres@scyphoshealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: security@scyphoshealth.com, procurement <procurement@scyphoshealth.com>, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 18:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit log extraction feasibility — Scyphos follow-up & questionnaire

Lina — perfect, thanks for the specifics. Quick responses and what we'll deliver: 

- Retention: we can support hot-window + cold archive. We'll implement a configurable lifecycle: 30 days (hot) then transition to cold S3 for remainder of retention (up to 2 years).
- Immutability: we can enable S3 Object Lock (Governance/Compliance mode) with customer-provided KMS; we'll include an option to set retention at object-level for 90 days or longer.
- Export format & schema: we'll provide JSONL with separate event-schema files for AdminActivity and APIRequest. Attached is a short example config (redwood_export_instructions.txt) and the questionnaire you sent (scyphos_audit_questions.xlsx) with a few filled responses.
- Delivery: daily bulk export to your S3 with SSE-KMS (you control keys) is supported; for high-priority forensic pulls we can provide an on-demand export API with an SLA target (proposed 4 hours for bulk retrieval).

Next steps (from Redwood):
1) I'll upload an anonymized sample export to the Drive link and share with security@ once it's ready (ETA: Tue 2027-06-29).
2) Schedule a 30m technical session with our infra solutions engineer (I proposed Wed 2027-06-30 at 10:00 AM PT and Thu 2027-07-01 at 9:00 AM PT — which works best for your team?).
3) We'll draft a short SOW addendum that outlines export frequency, retention, immutability option pricing, and retrieval SLA. Procurement can review after the technical sign-off.

Attachments: scyphos_audit_questions.xlsx (partially completed), redwood_export_instructions.txt

Thanks —
Ben
